title: Almost under control
purpose: Pay off the failed awning plan, reveal the emotional cost, and bring Yeti to an honest choice.
visual_action: Yeti stretches the detached awning across the cart lane. It catches all six berries, sags, and returns them together. The soft barrage rotates three displays, settles Tumble inside a purple banner, and leaves June gathering spilled blank slate signs. Mara catches one berry and calmly asks what happened. Yeti starts a reassuring answer, then actually looks at his friends.
conflict: Yeti can protect the appearance of competence for one more sentence or tell the truth and risk disappointment.
emotional_shift: Frantic defensiveness gives way to shame, empathy, and honesty.
props_out: six moonberries temporarily corralled at three points of the market
continuity_in: Mara, Yeti, Juniper, and Tumble match their creator-approved character references exactly.
Yeti carries the near end of the detached awning.
Juniper has chalk and sketch paper as scene props.
Every foreground and background character is barefoot or has uncovered natural bare paws.
continuity_out: No one is injured; Tumble’s official creator-approved design remains intact after the loose banner gag.
Yeti has stopped moving at center lane.
One berry bounces near each outer awning and four cluster by the moonberry stall.
Market displays are mussed, not broken.
transition_out: Sound narrows to awning flap and a single woodpecker tap before Yeti admits the full mistake.
